newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry seen investing $26.3 bln - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry seen investing $26.3 bln - CNI.

text.p: Brazilian industry is expected to invest $26.3 billion between 1995 and 1999, or 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said in a statement.

The CNI said the investments which have been carried out to date were mainly aimed at modernizing and cutting costs at existing installations, whereas future investments would focus on new plants and products.

The beverage, pharmaceutical, electrical material, communications material, food and transport material sectors planned to invest most, while the rubber, paper and mechanics sectors had the lowest investment plans, the CNI said.
The majority of the 730 companies surveyed by the CNI expect to see a large increase in their installed capacity. One third of the firms expect capacity to grow 50 percent by 1999.
The CNI survey found that 72 percent of the companies were more confident about the success of their investments since the anti-inflation Real Plan was introduced in July 1994.
The expectation of greater sales in the domestic market was the main factor compelling companies to invest, the CNI said.
((Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
